apps.description: The preinstalled Microsoft Teams app, one package shared by personal, work and school.

**Remove uninstalls the preinstalled Microsoft Teams app for every account on the PC, including accounts created later.**

Remove it only on a personal PC where nobody uses Teams for work or school.

tweaks.description: Keep Start search local by turning off Bing web results and search-box suggestions.
tweaks.info:
**Keeps Start search local: no Bing web results or search-box suggestions, and what you type stays on the PC.**

## Mechanism
- Three layers: the per-user search-box policy (every edition), the Bing setting the 24H2 search host still reads, and Microsoft's "Don't search the web" policy, which only Enterprise, Education and IoT editions honour.

## Drawbacks
- Web answers in the search box (conversions, definitions, quick lookups) stop.
- File Explorer stops suggesting and storing your recent searches, the only effect Microsoft documents for this policy.

## Caveats
- Feature updates often reset the Bing setting; the tweak then shows System Default while the policies still hold. Apply it again to restore all three.
- Some users report the taskbar search box disappearing with this policy (not confirmed on 24H2).

## Notes
- Works on every edition, including Home. Signing out, or restarting Explorer, also applies it.

## Related
- **Turn off search highlights** (Interface) removes promoted content from the search box; the two combine.

## Recommendation
Apply it if you use Start to open apps and settings. Skip it if you use the Start box as a web search bar.

## Sources

tweaks.description: Disable the WSearch service so Windows stops building and maintaining the file index.
tweaks.info:
**Turns off Windows Search indexing, so Windows stops building and maintaining its file index in the background.**

## Drawbacks
- File search in Explorer becomes a slow folder-by-folder scan.
- Start search for apps and settings gets slower and less complete; the Windows 11 taskbar search can return nothing.
- Classic Outlook search stops working.
- No measurable gain on a healthy SSD, where indexing uses under 1 percent idle CPU.

## Notes
- After reverting, the index rebuilds from scratch, which takes a while on a large profile.

## Recommendation
Worth it on a hard drive, a low-RAM PC, or if you search with a separate tool such as Everything. On a healthy SSD, leave it on.

## Sources

- [Guidelines for disabling system services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/security/windows-services/security-guidelines-for-disabling-system-services-in-windows-server)

tweaks.description: Disable the SysMain preloader so Windows stops profiling launches and warming the standby list.
tweaks.info:
**Turns off SysMain, the service that learns which apps you launch and preloads them into RAM. A targeted fix for SysMain pinning the disk at 100 percent, not a general speedup.**

## Drawbacks
- Apps start from disk instead of a warmed cache.
- No measurable gain on an SSD with enough RAM.

## Notes
- To revert, prefer System Default: it restores your PC's real prior start type.

## Related
- **Disable RAM memory compression** controls memory compression, which stays on with this tweak.

## Recommendation
Leave SysMain on unless you have confirmed it is causing sustained 100 percent disk use.

## Sources
- [Disable-MMAgent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/mmagent/disable-mmagent)
- [Guidelines for disabling system services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/security/windows-services/security-guidelines-for-disabling-system-services-in-windows-server)
tweaks.name: Disable SysMain (SuperFetch) prefetching
tweaks.warning: Microsoft recommends leaving SysMain on. Disable it only if SysMain is proven to spike disk usage on your machine. The Automatic start type offered here is the published stock value but has not been confirmed on a clean 24H2 image, so treat the restore path as best effort.

tweaks.description: Halve the CPU share MMCSS guarantees to low-priority tasks while a multimedia thread is registered.
tweaks.info:
**Halves the CPU share Windows reserves for background work while audio or video plays (from 20 to 10 percent), giving media threads more headroom under load.**

## Mechanism
- The Multimedia Class Scheduler holds this share back only while a media task, such as audio playback, is registered; at other times the value does nothing.

## Drawbacks
- Background streams or recordings can glitch under heavy load.
- No measured effect on game frame rates: it governs media threads, not your game.

## Related
- **Lift the multimedia network throttling cap** tunes a sibling setting; the two are independent.

## Recommendation
Worth setting on an audio production PC. Gamers should skip it.

## Sources
- [Multimedia Class Scheduler Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/multimedia-class-scheduler-service)
tweaks.name: Halve the MMCSS reserved CPU (System Responsiveness)

tweaks.description: Choose whether GPU frame scheduling runs on the GPU, on the CPU, or is left to the system and driver.
tweaks.info:
**Moves GPU frame scheduling from the CPU to a scheduler on the graphics card (HAGS). NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation requires it.**

## Drawbacks
- Uses slightly more video memory.
- Some VR users report stutter with it on.
- Outside Frame Generation, average FPS changes stay within run-to-run noise.

## Requirements
- A GPU driver of WDDM 2.7 or newer; on unsupported hardware the setting does nothing.

## Notes
- "Let the system decide" leaves the choice to Windows and the driver.
- GPU driver installs can rewrite this setting.

## Recommendation
Turn it on for DLSS Frame Generation or a CPU-limited system. Otherwise leave it as your PC shipped.

## Sources
- [Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware-accelerated-gpu-scheduling-4f5ba4a0-4b26-4f4e-8b4b-0a1e9a2b4d55)
- [How-To Geek: enable hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling](https://www.howtogeek.com/756935/how-to-enable-hardware-accelerated-gpu-scheduling-in-windows-11/)
tweaks.name: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (HAGS)
tweaks.warning: The factory value varies by OEM image and GPU driver, so neither option here is a return to how your machine shipped. If you are unsure which state it shipped in, leave this tweak alone and use Settings > System > Display > Graphics instead.

tweaks.description: Write the GameConfigStore values that force games onto the legacy exclusive fullscreen path.
tweaks.info:
**Tries to force every game onto the older exclusive fullscreen path instead of Windows' fullscreen optimizations. Whether these values really do that is unsettled.**

## Mechanism
- Writes three undocumented per-user game settings. Sources disagree on what each number means, and the forced option follows one of two conflicting community recipes.
- The other option writes the values found on an untouched Windows 11 24H2 PC.

## Drawbacks
- Black-screen flicker when switching tasks is common.
- No measured gain: on current Windows the exclusive path is usually equal or worse.

## Related
- It undermines **Variable refresh rate for windowed games** and **Turn on optimizations for windowed games**, which rely on the modern path.

## Recommendation
Only for troubleshooting one game that stutters in borderless mode, after trying its own fullscreen setting and the per-game "Disable fullscreen optimizations" checkbox. Check the result yourself in that game.

## Sources
- [Optimizations for windowed games in Windows 11](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/display-graphics/optimizations-for-windowed-games-in-windows-11)
- [Microsoft Q&A: fullscreen optimizations in the registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4079856/enable-or-disable-full-screen-optimizations-on-win)
- [Community recipes for fullscreen optimizations](https://deepwiki.com/shoober420/windows11-scripts/5.3-fullscreen-optimizations-and-hdr)
tweaks.name: Force exclusive fullscreen in games
tweaks.warning: Microsoft documents none of these three values and community sources disagree on their meaning. It is a global per-user override applied to every game, not a per-title fix, and it can break Auto HDR, variable refresh rate, and fast Alt-Tab. Prefer the per-game compatibility setting first.

tweaks.description: Set the VRROptimizeEnable field that extends adaptive sync to DX11 and borderless titles.
tweaks.info:
**Extends variable refresh rate (adaptive sync) to DirectX 11 and windowed or borderless games that do not drive it themselves, for smoother motion with less tearing.**

## Requirements
- An adaptive-sync (FreeSync or G-Sync compatible) display and GPU with a WDDM 2.6 or newer driver. On a fixed-refresh screen it does nothing.

## Notes
- The same switch as Settings > System > Display > Graphics. Only this setting changes; the other graphics settings stored with it are kept.
- "Off" and "Driver decides" both mean off: Settings writes the first once you have ever turned the feature on, and an untouched PC has the second.
- No frame-rate change, and some games act oddly with a frame cap.

## Related
- **Force exclusive fullscreen in games** bypasses the path this relies on.

## Recommendation
Turn it on if you have a FreeSync or G-Sync compatible display and play DX11 or borderless games.

## Sources
- [Optimizations for windowed games in Windows 11](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/display-graphics/optimizations-for-windowed-games-in-windows-11)
- [ElevenForum: variable refresh rate for games](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/enable-or-disable-variable-refresh-rate-for-games-in-windows-11.12052/)
tweaks.name: Variable refresh rate for windowed games

tweaks.description: Duplicate the hidden Ultimate Performance scheme and activate the copy, restoring your previous plan on revert.
tweaks.info:
**Creates a copy of Windows' hidden Ultimate Performance power plan and makes it active. Core parking and most CPU idle states are off, cutting ramp-up delays on a desktop.**

## Drawbacks
- A small difference over the High Performance plan; no published measurement shows higher average FPS.

## Caveats
- Changes you make to the created plan's settings are lost when reverting deletes it.
- **Disable USB selective suspend** and **Disable wake timers** (Network), applied while this plan is active, change only this plan and are lost with it.
- On Modern Standby laptops Windows may offer only Balanced, and the plan cannot be used.

## Notes
- Reverting reactivates the plan you had before (Balanced if that plan was deleted since) and deletes the copy.
- An Ultimate Performance copy you made yourself is never reused or deleted.

## Recommendation
Worth trying on a desktop on AC power where you want minimum latency. Skip it on a laptop or if you already use High Performance.

## Sources
- [Powercfg command-line options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options)
- [PowerDuplicateScheme](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/powrprof/nf-powrprof-powerduplicatescheme)
tweaks.name: Activate the Ultimate Performance power plan

options.label: Ultimate Performance

tweaks.warning: Keeps the CPU in high power states with core parking off, so idle power, heat, and fan noise rise continuously. On a laptop it costs real battery runtime for a difference you are unlikely to measure.

tweaks.description: Turn off Memory Integrity to recover CPU-bound frame times, at a critical cost to security.
tweaks.info:
**Turns off Memory Integrity (hypervisor-enforced code integrity) to recover CPU headroom, mostly in CPU-limited games on older processors. A critical security downgrade.**

## Drawbacks
- No hypervisor-enforced protection against kernel malware or malicious and vulnerable drivers.
- Some anti-cheat systems require Memory Integrity.
- The quoted 5 to 15 percent gains come from tech press, not Microsoft.

## Caveats
- VBS itself keeps running when Hyper-V, WSL2, Windows Sandbox or Credential Guard need it, so the gain is smaller than advertised.
- Windows turns Memory Integrity on by default only on clean Windows 11 installs on qualifying hardware. Choosing "Memory integrity enabled" turns it on even if your PC never had it, so check driver compatibility or revert with System Default instead.

## Recommendation
Only on a personal gaming PC where you knowingly accept weaker security, after confirming your anti-cheat allows it. Never on a work, shared or sensitive PC.

## Sources
- [Enable memory integrity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/enable-virtualization-based-protection-of-code-integrity)
- [Memory integrity and VBS enablement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/oem-hvci-enablement)
tweaks.name: Disable VBS and Memory Integrity (HVCI)
tweaks.warning: CRITICAL SECURITY DOWNGRADE. Conflicts directly with the security category's Credential Guard tweak: Credential Guard is VBS-hosted and cannot run once this is applied, so never enable both. This tweak does not touch WasEnabledBy, so the Windows Security memory integrity page may still read as administrator-managed after a revert, and if memory integrity was enabled with UEFI lock nothing changes until Secure Boot is disabled in firmware.

tweaks.description: Write the KB4073119 override pair that disables the Spectre v2 and Meltdown mitigations.
tweaks.info:
**Removes the Spectre variant 2 and Meltdown CPU mitigations to reclaim throughput on older processors. A critical security downgrade.**

## Drawbacks
- Re-exposes attacks that read memory across process and virtual machine boundaries.
- Intel CPUs from roughly the 10th generation and all AMD CPUs never had the Meltdown mitigation on, so half of this does nothing there.
- Some benchmarks get worse after disabling; measure your own workload.

## Notes
- Other mitigations (MDS, L1TF, Downfall and more) stay on.
- To revert, prefer System Default: it puts back any override that was there before.

## Recommendation
Hard to justify on modern hardware. Only on an isolated, older, personal PC where you knowingly accept the risk.

## Sources
- [KB4073119: speculative execution side-channel guidance](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/kb4073119-windows-client-guidance-for-it-pros-to-protect-against-silicon-based-microarchitectural-and-speculative-execution-side-channel-vulnerabilities-35820a8a-ae13-1299-88cc-357f104f5b11)
- [KVA Shadow: mitigating Meltdown on Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/msrc/blog/2018/03/kva-shadow-mitigating-meltdown-on-windows)
tweaks.name: Disable Spectre / Meltdown CPU mitigations

options.label: Spectre v2 and Meltdown mitigations disabled

tweaks.warning: CRITICAL SECURITY DOWNGRADE. FeatureSettingsOverride is a single DWORD, so writing 3 overwrites any other mitigation override already configured, including the 0x2000000 value KB5029778 specifies for the Downfall (Gather Data Sampling) mitigation. Reverting to absent likewise deletes an administrator's deliberate setting. Check the current value before applying this on a managed machine.

tweaks.description: Set the pointer ballistics values to 0 for a strict 1:1 mouse-to-cursor mapping.
tweaks.info:
**Turns off Enhance Pointer Precision, so the cursor moves in step with the mouse: the same motion always covers the same distance.**

## Drawbacks
- Crossing a large or multi-monitor desktop takes more physical movement.

## Caveats
- Games that read raw mouse input already ignore this, so it may only change the desktop cursor.
- A custom acceleration curve is not reset.

## Notes
- Takes effect after you sign out and back in; no restart is needed.

## Recommendation
Recommended for gamers, especially in shooters. Leave it on if you like the accelerated feel on a large desktop.

## Sources
- [KB Q149228: how to disable mouse acceleration](https://jeffpar.github.io/kbarchive/kb/149/Q149228/)
- [TenForums: Enhance Pointer Precision](https://www.tenforums.com/tutorials/101691-turn-off-enhance-pointer-precision-windows.html)
tweaks.name: Disable mouse acceleration (Enhance Pointer Precision)

tweaks.description: Cap Windows diagnostic data at the Required level instead of the full optional level.
tweaks.info:
**Caps Windows diagnostic data at the Required level for every account, so optional data such as app usage and inking samples is no longer sent, and Settings can no longer raise it.**

## Drawbacks
- The diagnostic data switch in Settings is greyed out until you revert.

## Caveats
- Required diagnostic data is still sent: this is a cap, not an off switch, and the telemetry service keeps running.
- Windows Insider builds raise the level again regardless of this setting.

## Notes
- User's choice removes the policy, so the Settings switch works again.
- Takes effect immediately.

## Related
- **Disable User Experiences and Telemetry (DiagTrack)** (Services) stops the service that sends the data.

## Recommendation
Worth applying on any personal PC. Hold off while Microsoft support is helping you with an update or crash problem.

- [Policy CSP - System](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-system)
- [Configure Windows diagnostic data in your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/configure-windows-diagnostic-data-in-your-organization)

tweaks.description: Opt out of the Customer Experience Improvement Program and disable its upload tasks.
tweaks.info:
**Opts this PC out of the Customer Experience Improvement Program, an older Microsoft data program, and disables its scheduled upload tasks.**

## Mechanism
- Sets the opt-out policy and disables the program's Consolidator and USB tasks, the older kernel task where it exists, and the Sqm-Tasks collector that gathers TPM and Secure Boot data.

## Caveats
- This is not a control for modern Windows telemetry, which is sent by a different service.
- On a PC that never joined the program, the tasks already do nothing, so only the opt-out policy matters.

## Notes
- A feature update may turn the tasks back on; the opt-out policy stays.
- Reverting restores each task's previous state; it does not force them on.

## Related
- **Disable Autochk Proxy task** (Services) covers another uploader for this program.
- **Limit diagnostic data to the Required level** is the control for modern diagnostic data.

## Sources
- [CEIPEnable (Microsoft)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/devnotes/ceipenable)
- [Manage connections from Windows to Microsoft services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services)

tweaks.description: Stop the Application Experience appraiser and inventory telemetry tasks and their policies.
tweaks.info:
**Stops the Compatibility Appraiser (CompatTelRunner.exe), which regularly scans your installed apps to report upgrade readiness to Microsoft, and turns off its app inventory collection.**

## Caveats
- Windows Update uses this data to hold back feature updates that would break an app or driver, so such problems are less likely to be caught first.
- Feature updates turn the tasks back on; the switch then shows System Default until you apply it again.
- The compatibility database update task in the same folder is left alone: it keeps app compatibility fixes current and is not telemetry.

## Notes
- The often-reported CPU and disk savings have not been measured by Microsoft or any benchmark.
- Do not delete CompatTelRunner.exe yourself: Windows restores it, and removing it has broken updates.

## Related
- **Disable app and device inventory collectors** covers the newer 24H2 collectors.

## Recommendation
Apply it on a PC you keep on its current Windows version. Hold off before a feature upgrade, when these checks work in your favour.

## Sources
- [DISA STIG V-253385: Application Compatibility Program Inventory](https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft_windows_11/2022-06-24/finding/V-253385)
- [Configure Windows diagnostic data in your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/configure-windows-diagnostic-data-in-your-organization)
tweaks.name: Disable Compatibility Appraiser tasks

tweaks.description: Stop Windows collecting and publishing your activity history.
tweaks.info:
**Stops Windows recording a history of what you do on this PC, and stops it publishing or uploading that history to your account, for every account.**

## Notes
- On Windows 11, Timeline and cloud upload of activity history are already gone, so the change is small. On Windows 10, Timeline stops working.
- History already stored is not deleted; clear it in Settings > Privacy & security > Activity history.
- The Settings switches are locked while this is applied. Takes effect immediately.

tweaks.info:
**Turns off location for the whole PC, so neither Windows nor any app can find where you are, and locks the Location page in Settings.**

## Drawbacks
- Automatic time zone stops working, so the clock can be wrong after you travel.
- Find My Device can no longer locate the PC.
- Weather, Maps and other location apps need you to enter a place by hand.

- Takes effect immediately; reopen Settings to see the change.

- **Turn off Find My Device** has nothing left to do while this is applied.

Suits a desktop that never needs its location. Skip it on a laptop you travel with.

tweaks.description: Strip the ads, tips, and fun facts off the Spotlight lock screen while keeping the pictures.
tweaks.info:
**Keeps the Windows Spotlight pictures on your lock screen but removes the ads, tips and fun facts shown over them.**

- The captions saying where a photo was taken go too.

tweaks.description: Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences by policy (honored on Enterprise, Education, and IoT only).
tweaks.info:
**Turns off Microsoft's consumer extras by policy: apps installed automatically after setup, promoted Start tiles and membership notifications.**

## Requirements
- Works only on Enterprise, Education and IoT Enterprise (including LTSC). On Home and Pro it does nothing at all.

tweaks.description: Stop Windows handing your full language list to web content.
tweaks.info:
**Stops Windows telling websites which languages you have set up, one small signal used to fingerprint your browser.**

- Modern browsers send their own language list, so the effect is mostly on web content built into Windows.
- Some multilingual sites may stop picking your language automatically.
- Only your account changes. Browsers pick it up the next time they start.

- [Manage connections from Windows to Microsoft services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services)

**Stops File Explorer asking Microsoft's cloud for file suggestions based on your account activity, such as recent OneDrive and SharePoint files, for every account.**

tweaks.description: Disable the Windows Error Reporting service so crash reports are never collected.
tweaks.info:
**Disables the Windows Error Reporting service, so crash and hang reports are not collected, queued or sent at all.**

## Drawbacks
- Reliability Monitor's crash history goes quiet, and some third-party crash handlers behave differently.
- It does not make Windows faster.

## Notes
- A running instance keeps running until the next restart.
- Reverting restores the service's previous start type.

## Related
- **Disable Windows Error Reporting** sets the reporting policy; the natural pair.
- **Disable Windows Error Reporting QueueReporting task** (Services) stops queued reports being uploaded.

## Recommendation
Use it on a stable PC. Leave it alone while you are troubleshooting crashes.

- [WER settings (Microsoft)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/wer/wer-settings)
tweaks.name: Disable the Windows Error Reporting service

tweaks.description: Disable the Remote Registry service so this PC's registry cannot be edited from the network.
tweaks.info:
**Disables the Remote Registry service, so no one can read or edit this PC's registry over the network, whatever credentials they hold.**

## Drawbacks
- Remote management agents, inventory tools and some backup checks that read the registry from another PC stop working.

## Notes
- Windows already ships this service Disabled, so on most PCs the tweak shows as applied and nothing changes.
- The app does not stop a running instance; if something had started it, it stops at the next restart.
- Reverting restores the start type recorded before you applied.

## Related
- **Restrict remote SAM calls to administrators**, **Disable administrative shares** and **Disable WinRM remoting** close other remote channels.

## Recommendation
Apply it on any home or standalone PC. Skip it only if software manages this PC's registry from another computer.

## Sources
- [Remote Registry service defaults in Windows 11 (revertservice)](https://revertservice.com/11/remoteregistry/)
- [Remote Registry, Windows 11 service (batcmd)](https://batcmd.com/windows/11/services/remoteregistry/)
tweaks.name: Disable the Remote Registry service

tweaks.description: Remove the legacy SMBv1 file-sharing protocol exploited by WannaCry and EternalBlue.
tweaks.info:
**Removes SMBv1, the obsolete file-sharing protocol behind the WannaCry and EternalBlue attacks. Modern file sharing (SMB 2 and 3) is unaffected.**

## Mechanism
- Disables the `SMB1Protocol` Windows feature, which removes both the SMBv1 client and server.
- Also sets the server switch `SMB1 = 0`, so the SMBv1 server stays off even if the feature comes back.

## Notes
- Removing or reinstalling the feature can take several minutes and finishes at the next restart.
- Where the feature is already off (most Windows 11 PCs), applying only sets the server switch and never touches the feature, so reverting cannot install SMBv1.

## Related
- **Require SMB signing**, **Disable SMB insecure guest logons** and **Block NTLM on the SMB client** cause the same kind of old-NAS breakage; apply them together and test old storage once.

## Recommendation
Apply it; SMBv1 has no place on today's networks. Hold off only if you still use hardware that speaks nothing newer, and plan to replace it.

## Sources
- [Detect, enable, and disable SMBv1, SMBv2, and SMBv3](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/troubleshoot/detect-enable-and-disable-smbv1-v2-v3)
- [SMBv1 is not installed by default](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/troubleshoot/smbv1-not-installed-by-default-in-windows)
tweaks.name: Remove SMBv1 protocol
tweaks.warning: Very old SMB1-only NAS boxes, USB-router shares, and Windows XP or 2003 hosts become unreachable. SMBv1 is not installed by default on Windows 11, nor on Windows 10 except the Home and Pro editions.

tweaks.description: Stop auto-creation of the hidden administrative shares to hamper lateral movement.
tweaks.info:
**Stops Windows recreating the hidden `C$`, `D$` and `ADMIN$` shares that remote tools and attackers with stolen admin passwords use to copy files onto a PC.**

## Mechanism
- Sets `AutoShareWks = 0`, so the Server service skips creating the shares when it starts. `IPC$` and shares you created are untouched.

## Caveats
- Unverified on Windows 11 24H2: the registry value may no longer be honoured there. After the reboot, run `net share` to confirm the shares are gone.
- Microsoft advises against removing these shares because it can break many things.

## Related
- **Filter the remote local-admin token** already blocks most use of these shares by local accounts.
- **Restrict remote SAM calls to administrators** is another lateral-movement control.

## Recommendation
Fine on a standalone personal PC that never uses these shares. Avoid it if you rely on remote admin tools, network backup agents or PsExec-style management.

## Sources
- [Remove administrative shares](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/remove-administrative-shares)
tweaks.name: Disable administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$)
tweaks.warning: Breaks remote admin tools, some backup software, and PsExec or remote-WMI workflows that rely on C$ and ADMIN$. An administrator can recreate the shares, so this is friction rather than a boundary.

tweaks.description: Turn on the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist to stop bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver attacks.
tweaks.info:
**Makes Windows refuse to load kernel drivers on Microsoft's list of known-vulnerable drivers, which attackers bring along to switch off security software.**

## Caveats
- Microsoft documents the feature but not this registry value; it rests on community sources, so a future build could stop honouring it.
- A blocked legitimate driver can make a device or tool malfunction, and in rare cases cause a blue screen.
- While memory integrity, Smart App Control or S mode is on, the blocklist is forced on and this value has no say.

## Notes
- On by default since Windows 11 22H2, so this usually pins the current state.
- Not configured deletes the value and hands control back to the Windows Security toggle (Device security > Core isolation), which is on by default.

## Related
- **Disable VBS and Memory Integrity (HVCI)** (Performance): once memory integrity is off, this value is what keeps the blocklist on. The two combine well.

## Recommendation
Apply it. If a device stops working after the reboot, check whether its driver is on the list before reverting.

## Sources
- [Microsoft recommended driver block rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules)
- [Enable or disable the vulnerable driver blocklist (Eleven Forum)](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/enable-or-disable-microsoft-vulnerable-driver-blocklist-in-windows-11.10031/)
tweaks.name: Enable the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist

tweaks.description: Turn on Defender Controlled Folder Access to block unauthorized apps writing to protected folders.
tweaks.info:
**Blocks unrecognised apps from changing files in Documents, Pictures, Desktop and your other protected folders: Windows' built-in ransomware shield.**

## Mechanism
- Defender checks every change to a file in a protected folder against its list of trusted apps; untrusted apps are refused and you get a notification.
- Audit only logs what would have been blocked, without blocking anything.

## Caveats
- The app confirms the policy was set, not that the feature engaged; `Get-MpPreference` shows the effective setting.
- On Intune or Configuration Manager PCs, their policies overwrite this.

## Requirements
- Microsoft Defender must be the active antivirus; with a third-party antivirus this does nothing.

## Notes
- Allow a blocked app, or add folders, in Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Ransomware protection.

## Related
- **Enforce SmartScreen (apps and Edge)** and **Enable PUA/PUP protection** together with this make a noticeably stricter PC.

## Recommendation
Worth it if you want ransomware protection and are willing to allow apps when something is blocked. Start with Audit only for a week, check what it caught, then switch to Block.

tweaks.description: Block external Thunderbolt and PCIe peripherals from touching memory before you sign in.

## Related

tweaks.description: Choose how Windows Update behaves: install automatically, download only, notify only, or off by policy.
tweaks.info:
**Sets how Windows Update handles updates: install automatically, download only, notify only, or off by policy.**

## Mechanism
- **Automatic**: downloads and installs on Windows' default daily schedule.
- **Download only**: downloads in the background, then tells you updates are ready to install.
- **Notify only**: nothing downloads until you start it from Settings.
- **Off by policy**: no automatic updates; you check and install from Settings yourself.

## Caveats
- **Off by policy** is not a full block: the update services keep running, Check for updates still works, and other parts of Windows can still start scans.
- **Automatic** is not the same as no policy: it locks a daily install schedule, where an unmanaged PC uses Microsoft's own install-and-restart behaviour.

## Notes
- Reverting removes the policy, and your own Settings choices apply again.
- Takes effect at the next update scan, with no restart.

## Related
- **Block auto-restart while signed in** works only with Automatic.
- **Block the Windows Update pipeline** is the full off switch. With both, pick Notify only here: Off by policy disables the pipeline's server redirect.

## Recommendation
Notify only is the balanced choice for a Pro PC you actually maintain. If patches could pile up unattended, stay on Automatic.

tweaks.description: Stop Windows Update at the source: the services, every scan and notification task, the update UI, and the Medic service that undoes exactly this kind of change.
tweaks.info:
**Shuts Windows Update down completely: its services, its scan and reminder tasks, the update page in Settings and the network path to Microsoft. It also disables the Medic service that would otherwise undo the block.**

## Mechanism
- Disables the Windows Update Medic service and its tasks first, since they re-enable update services that were turned off.
- Disables every task that starts an update scan or shows the "missing important updates" prompt.
- Removes Check for updates and update notifications by policy, and points scans at a local address where nothing answers.
- Disables the Windows Update and Update Orchestrator services last.

## Caveats
- **The Microsoft Store may break.** Microsoft says one of these policies can stop Store and Delivery Optimization connections, and a disabled update service is a known cause of Store error 0x80070422. Not tested here.
- **The block may not last.** A Windows repair tool (`upfc.exe`) is reported to reset the update services roughly every five days; this tweak does not handle it. Check that the block still holds after a week.
- Defender definitions lose the Windows Update route; Defender's own update channel should keep working (not tested).
- Programs that use the Windows Update API stop working.
- It overwrites any WSUS or organization update server setting; never apply it on a managed PC.

## Requirements
- Services and tasks are blocked on every edition; Home ignores the policy parts (Settings page, notifications, server redirect).
- Needs the TrustedInstaller service; without it the tweak shows as not available.

## Notes
- Restart after reverting too: some re-enabled tasks do not re-arm until then.
- Other Windows Update tweaks sit idle while this is applied and take effect again when it is reverted.

## Related
- **Windows Update mode**: pick Notify only there, not Off by policy, which switches off this tweak's server redirect.
- **Defer feature updates** and **Defer quality updates**, applied beforehand, control what installs when the block is lifted.

## Recommendation
Only for a PC you patch some other way: offline, a lab machine, or one you patch by hand. Revert it at least monthly to install updates. For everyday control, use Windows Update mode on Notify only instead.
